h1: Playground Amenities for Real Estate Projects: A Builder's Planning Guide

props.title: Playground Amenities for Real Estate Projects: A Builder's Planning Guide
props.summaryText: For builders and project managers: when to bring the play area into the plan, how to size it, what to include for each project type, and how to hand it over so it still looks good years later.
props.author: ananya-kulkarni
props.imageAlt: Tepee play towers with slides and a net bridge between residential towers

takeaways.text: Bring the play area into the site plan at the design stage, not into leftover space after the layout is fixed.
Size it by the number of families expected, with safety zones, not by the space left over.
Install after heavy construction traffic has finished, but early enough to show buyers on site visits.
Hand over with drawings, warranty documents, a maintenance guide and supplier contacts.

faq.q: When should a builder plan the playground?
faq.a: At the site planning and landscape design stage, alongside levels, drainage and services. That ensures the play area gets a good location, enough space, sunlight and access, and avoids clashes with podium structures or utilities.

faq.q: What playground amenities should a residential project include?
faq.a: Usually a main play structure for 5 to 12-year-olds, a toddler zone, swings, a few simple items like spring riders, an outdoor gym for adults, seating and shade, lighting, and safety surfacing. Large townships add themed or nature play areas and multiple zones.

faq.q: When should playground equipment be installed in a construction project?
faq.a: After heavy construction traffic around the area has finished and landscaping levels are ready, but early enough for a show area or before possession. Coordinate with the landscape contractor on surfacing and drainage.

faq.q: What should a builder hand over to the society?
faq.a: Layout drawings, product details, warranty documents, the maintenance and inspection guide, records of installation, and supplier contacts for spares and service.
